1	# Industry Pack — Mobile Android (Material 3 Expressive)
2	
3	For Android apps built with Jetpack Compose or XML views, and Flutter apps using
4	Material widgets. Anchored to **Material 3 Expressive**, announced at the
5	**Android Show I/O Edition** on **May 13, 2025**, with general availability in
6	2025–2026 across Android 16, Wear OS 6, and Material Components.
7	
8	Reference points: Google's flagship apps (Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps,
9	Messages, Drive, YouTube), **Material You** showcases, **Linear Android**,
10	**Notion Android**, **Spotify**, **Twitter/X**, **TickTick, Todoist**, **Pocket
11	Casts, Plex, Tasker, Microsoft Outlook for Android**.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Pack Identity
16	
17	Material 3 Expressive emphasizes:
18	
19	- **Spring-based motion** as the default (replacing fixed easing curves)
20	- **Shape morphing** — components change shape on press (pill → rounded square)
21	- **Larger, bolder typography** with weight variation as the primary hierarchy
22	  driver (Bold over Big)
23	- **Color expressiveness** via dynamic Material You palette generation
24	- **Floating Toolbars / FAB Menus** replacing bottom app bars
25	- **Pill-shaped buttons** as the new default
26	- **5 button sizes** (XS / S / M / L / XL)
27	- **48dp minimum tap target** (always)
28	- **Navigation bar now 64dp** (down from 80dp in Material 3 stock)
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Token Overrides
33	
34	```css
35	:root[data-pack="android"] {
36	  /* M3 dynamic color — use the user's wallpaper-based primary by default */
37	  --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.16 280);          /* default purple, will be overridden by Material You */
38	  --color-accent-fg: oklch(99% 0.01 280);
39	  --color-accent-soft: oklch(95% 0.04 280);
40	  --color-accent-strong: oklch(50% 0.18 280);
41	
42	  /* M3 radii */
43	  --radius-button: 9999px;                      /* pill */
44	  --radius-input: 0.25rem;                      /* 4dp */
45	  --radius-card: 0.75rem;                       /* 12dp */
46	  --radius-modal: 1.75rem;                      /* 28dp - M3 modal corner */
47	  --radius-bottomsheet: 1.75rem;                /* 28dp top corner only */
48	
49	  /* Roboto Flex variable */
50	  --font-sans: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;
51	  --font-display: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;
52	
53	  /* M3 leading */
54	  --leading-display: 1.12;
55	  --leading-headline: 1.25;
56	  --leading-title: 1.4;
57	  --leading-body: 1.45;
58	  --leading-label: 1.3;
59	}
60	```
61	
62	For pure Material You (wallpaper-driven):
63	```css
64	:root[data-pack="android-you"] {
65	  --color-accent: oklch(var(--m3-primary));     /* sourced from system at runtime */
66	}
67	```
68	
69	---
70	
71	## The Material 3 Color System
72	
73	M3 introduces **roles** instead of named colors. Each role has an `on*` companion
74	(for text/icon on that surface) and `*-container` variants (for backgrounds that
75	sit on top of the base).
76	
77	### Primary palette
78	
79	```
80	primary               — primary brand surface color (e.g., FAB background)
81	onPrimary             — text/icon on primary
82	primaryContainer      — softer container holding primary content
83	onPrimaryContainer    — text on primary container
84	```
85	
86	Same pattern for `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `inverseSurface`.
87	
88	### Full M3 Color Roles
89	
90	```
91	primary, onPrimary, primaryContainer, onPrimaryContainer
92	secondary, onSecondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer
93	tertiary, onTertiary, tertiaryContainer, onTertiaryContainer
94	error, onError, errorContainer, onErrorContainer
95	background, onBackground
96	surface, onSurface
97	surfaceVariant, onSurfaceVariant
98	surfaceDim, surfaceBright
99	surfaceContainerLowest, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer,
100	  surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest
101	inverseSurface, inverseOnSurface, inversePrimary
102	outline, outlineVariant
103	scrim, shadow
104	```
105	
106	13-tone palettes generate these from a single source color. With **Material You**,
107	that source color comes from the user's wallpaper at runtime.
108	
109	### 3:1 contrast minimum for roles
110	
111	All `on*` colors guarantee 3:1 contrast against their base. For body text use
112	`onSurface` on `surface` (always passes 4.5:1).
113	
114	### In Compose
115	
116	```kotlin
117	MaterialTheme(
118	  colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme(),
119	  typography = Typography(),
120	) {
121	  Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface) {
122	    Text("Hello", color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface)
123	  }
124	}
125	```
126	
127	For dynamic Material You:
128	```kotlin
129	val colorScheme = when {
130	  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
131	    if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
132	    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
133	  }
134	  isSystemInDarkTheme() -> darkColorScheme()
135	  else -> lightColorScheme()
136	}
137	```
138	
139	---
140	
141	## Typography — The 15-Token Scale
142	
143	M3 has 15 typography tokens (5 roles × 3 sizes). Apply via `MaterialTheme.typography`.
144	
145	| Token | Size | Weight | Line height | Letter spacing |
146	|---|---|---|---|---|
147	| **Display Large** | 57sp | Regular 400 | 64sp | -0.25 |
148	| **Display Medium** | 45sp | Regular 400 | 52sp | 0 |
149	| **Display Small** | 36sp | Regular 400 | 44sp | 0 |
150	| **Headline Large** | 32sp | Regular 400 | 40sp | 0 |
151	| **Headline Medium** | 28sp | Regular 400 | 36sp | 0 |
152	| **Headline Small** | 24sp | Regular 400 | 32sp | 0 |
153	| **Title Large** | 22sp | Regular 400 | 28sp | 0 |
154	| **Title Medium** | 16sp | Medium 500 | 24sp | 0.15 |
155	| **Title Small** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
156	| **Body Large** | 16sp | Regular 400 | 24sp | 0.5 |
157	| **Body Medium** | 14sp | Regular 400 | 20sp | 0.25 |
158	| **Body Small** | 12sp | Regular 400 | 16sp | 0.4 |
159	| **Label Large** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
160	| **Label Medium** | 12sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |
161	| **Label Small** | 11sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |
162	
163	In Compose:
164	```kotlin
165	Text("Title", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
166	Text("Body copy", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
167	Text("Button", style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge)
168	```
169	
170	### Roboto Flex variable
171	
172	M3 Expressive (2025) ships **Roboto Flex** as the primary typeface — variable axes:
173	- Weight: 100–1000
174	- Width: 25–151%
175	- Optical size: 8–144
176	- Slant, grade, ascender height, descender depth, counter width, all variable
177	
178	The "Bold over Big" principle: use weight (500 → 700) to convey hierarchy on the
179	same scale, instead of jumping size tokens.
180	
181	### Display Flexible Variants (M3 Expressive only)
182	
183	New in 2025: "Display Medium Flexible" and "Display Large Flexible" let apps use
184	larger, more expressive typography for product moments. Used in Google's flagship
185	apps for empty states, onboarding, hero moments.
186	
187	---
188	
189	## Buttons — 5 Sizes, 5 Styles
190	
191	M3 Expressive ships **5 button sizes** and **5 button styles**.
192	
193	### Sizes
194	
195	| Size | Height | Use |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| **XS** | 32dp | Inline, dense lists, chips-adjacent |
198	| **S** | 36dp | Secondary actions in tight spaces |
199	| **M** | 40dp | Default |
200	| **L** | 48dp | Primary actions, mobile CTAs |
201	| **XL** | 56dp | Hero CTAs, "Continue" in onboarding |
202	
203	```kotlin
204	Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Default M") }
205	Button(onClick = { }, modifier = Modifier.height(48.dp)) { Text("L") }
206	Button(
207	  onClick = { },
208	  modifier = Modifier.height(56.dp),
209	  contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 24.dp),
210	) { Text("XL") }
211	```
212	
213	### Styles
214	
215	| Style | Background | Use |
216	|---|---|---|
217	| **Filled** | `primary` | Primary action per screen |
218	| **Filled Tonal** | `secondaryContainer` | Co-equal action, softer than filled |
219	| **Elevated** | `surface` + shadow | Action that needs to lift off background |
220	| **Outlined** | transparent + outline | Secondary action |
221	| **Text** | transparent | Lowest-emphasis action, links |
222	
223	```kotlin
224	Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Filled") }              // primary
225	FilledTonalButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Tonal") }    // secondary
226	ElevatedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Elevated") }
227	OutlinedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Outlined") }
228	TextButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Text") }
229	```
230	
231	### Pill shape default, shape-morphs on press
232	
233	M3 Expressive defaults all buttons to pill shape. On press, the shape morphs to
234	a slightly more rounded square via spring animation. The default is enabled when
235	using `ButtonDefaults.shape`.
236	
237	```kotlin
238	Button(
239	  onClick = { },
240	  shape = ButtonDefaults.shape       // pill, morphs on press
241	) { Text("Action") }
242	```
243	
244	### Icon buttons
245	
246	```kotlin
247	IconButton(onClick = { }) {
248	  Icon(Icons.Default.Settings, contentDescription = "Settings")
249	}
250	
251	// Toggleable
252	IconToggleButton(checked = isChecked, onCheckedChange = { isChecked = it }) {
253	  Icon(
254	    if (isChecked) Icons.Filled.Favorite else Icons.Outlined.FavoriteBorder,
255	    contentDescription = "Like"
256	  )
257	}
258	```
259	
260	48dp tap target minimum. Always provide `contentDescription` for TalkBack.
261	
262	---
263	
264	## Navigation Bar (Bottom Nav)
265	
266	Material 3 Expressive: **64dp height** (reduced from M3 standard 80dp). Active
267	indicator: 56dp pill behind the selected icon.
268	
269	```kotlin
270	NavigationBar(modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp)) {
271	  navItems.forEach { item ->
272	    NavigationBarItem(
273	      icon = { Icon(item.icon, contentDescription = item.label) },
274	      label = { Text(item.label) },
275	      selected = currentRoute == item.route,
276	      onClick = { navigate(item.route) }
277	    )
278	  }
279	}
280	```
281	
282	### Behaviors
283	
284	- Active label not bold by default (M3 Expressive change — was bold in original M3).
285	- Labels always visible (selected and unselected).
286	- 3–5 items max. >5 items: use Navigation Drawer or Navigation Rail.
287	
288	### Material You Color
289	
290	Selected item indicator uses `secondaryContainer`. Icons use `onSurfaceVariant`
291	(unselected) → `onSecondaryContainer` (selected).
292	
293	---
294	
295	## Top App Bars
296	
297	Four variants:
298	
299	| Variant | Height | Use |
300	|---|---|---|
301	| **Small** | 64dp | Default for nested screens |
302	| **Center-aligned Small** | 64dp | Title centered (Material You style) |
303	| **Medium Flexible** | ~112dp | Important pages with extra space |
304	| **Large Flexible** | ~152dp | Hero pages, top-level destinations |
305	
306	```kotlin
307	// Small top app bar
308	TopAppBar(
309	  title = { Text("Inbox") },
310	  navigationIcon = {
311	    IconButton(onClick = { /* back */ }) {
312	      Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowBack, contentDescription = "Back")
313	    }
314	  },
315	  actions = {
316	    IconButton(onClick = { /* search */ }) {
317	      Icon(Icons.Default.Search, contentDescription = "Search")
318	    }
319	  }
320	)
321	
322	// Large top app bar that collapses on scroll
323	LargeTopAppBar(
324	  title = { Text("Inbox", style = MaterialTheme.typography.displaySmall) },
325	  scrollBehavior = scrollBehavior
326	)
327	```
328	
329	### Scroll behaviors
330	
331	- `pinnedScrollBehavior` — stays at top
332	- `enterAlwaysScrollBehavior` — collapses on scroll down, reappears on scroll up
333	- `exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior` — collapses to small variant, large only at top
334	
335	Large Flexible is the equivalent of iOS's "large title" — big at top, collapses
336	to small on scroll.
337	
338	---
339	
340	## Bottom Sheets
341	
342	Two variants:
343	
344	### Standard Bottom Sheet
345	
346	Inline with content (e.g., Google Maps location details). Always visible at
347	collapsed state, expands on drag.
348	
349	```kotlin
350	BottomSheetScaffold(
351	  sheetContent = { LocationDetails() },
352	  sheetPeekHeight = 128.dp,
353	) { padding ->
354	  MapView(padding)
355	}
356	```
357	
358	### Modal Bottom Sheet
359	
360	Overlay with scrim. Used for actions, filters, share sheets.
361	
362	```kotlin
363	val sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState()
364	val coroutineScope = rememberCoroutineScope()
365	
366	ModalBottomSheet(
367	  onDismissRequest = { coroutineScope.launch { sheetState.hide() } },
368	  sheetState = sheetState,
369	  dragHandle = { BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle() }
370	) {
371	  FilterContent()
372	}
373	```
374	
375	Rounded top corners (28dp). Drag handle visible by default. Swipe-down dismisses.
376	
377	---
378	
379	## FAB and FAB Menu (NEW in M3 Expressive)
380	
381	### Floating Action Button
382	
383	```kotlin
384	FloatingActionButton(onClick = { compose() }) {
385	  Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, contentDescription = "Compose")
386	}
387	
388	// Extended (with text)
389	ExtendedFloatingActionButton(
390	  onClick = { compose() },
391	  icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, null) },
392	  text = { Text("Compose") }
393	)
394	
395	// Small / Large variants
396	SmallFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
397	LargeFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
398	```
399	
400	### FAB Menu (NEW)
401	
402	When a single action isn't enough, FAB expands into a menu of secondary actions.
403	M3 Expressive introduces this as a stock component.
404	
405	```kotlin
406	FloatingActionButtonMenu(
407	  expanded = expanded,
408	  button = {
409	    ToggleFloatingActionButton(
410	      checked = expanded,
411	      onCheckedChange = { expanded = it }
412	    ) {
413	      Icon(Icons.Default.Add, null)
414	    }
415	  }
416	) {
417	  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Email, null) }, text = { Text("Email") })
418	  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Call, null) }, text = { Text("Call") })
419	  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Message, null) }, text = { Text("Message") })
420	}
421	```
422	
423	Replaces the older "speed dial" pattern.
424	
425	---
426	
427	## Toolbars — Docked and Floating (NEW)
428	
429	M3 Expressive deprecates the Bottom App Bar in favor of:
430	
431	### Docked Toolbar
432	
433	```kotlin
434	DockedToolbar(
435	  modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp),
436	  navigationIcon = { IconButton(...) { Icon(...) } },
437	  actions = {
438	    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, null) }
439	    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.MoreVert, null) }
440	  }
441	)
442	```
443	
444	### Floating Toolbar
445	
446	Translucent material, floats above content like iOS Liquid Glass equivalent.
447	
448	```kotlin
449	FloatingToolbar(
450	  modifier = Modifier
451	    .align(Alignment.BottomCenter)
452	    .padding(16.dp)
453	) {
454	  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatBold, null) }
455	  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatItalic, null) }
456	  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatUnderlined, null) }
457	}
458	```
459	
460	Use for: text editor formatting bars, contextual action sets, media player controls.
461	
462	---
463	
464	## Lists
465	
466	### List Item Spec (M3)
467	
468	| Lines | Height (no avatar) | Height (with avatar) |
469	|---|---|---|
470	| 1 line | 48dp | 56dp |
471	| 2 lines | 64dp | 72dp |
472	| 3 lines | 88dp | 88dp |
473	
474	Always 16dp horizontal padding.
475	
476	```kotlin
477	ListItem(
478	  headlineContent = { Text("Project Apollo") },
479	  supportingContent = { Text("Last updated 3 hours ago") },
480	  leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Folder, null) },
481	  trailingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.ChevronRight, null) },
482	  modifier = Modifier.clickable { open() }
483	)
484	```
485	
486	### Dividers
487	
488	Use `HorizontalDivider()` between sections, not between every item. Material 3
489	deprecated the always-divided list in favor of section-only dividers.
490	
491	---
492	
493	## Motion — Springs Replace Easing
494	
495	M3 Expressive replaces fixed-duration easing with **spring physics tokens** as the
496	default for important transitions.
497	
498	### Spring tokens
499	
500	```kotlin
501	// In Compose, the default for state animations
502	spring<Float>(
503	  dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy,
504	  stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMedium
505	)
506	
507	// Categories
508	Spring.DampingRatioHighBouncy
509	Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy
510	Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy
511	Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy
512	
513	Spring.StiffnessHigh
514	Spring.StiffnessMedium
515	Spring.StiffnessMediumLow
516	Spring.StiffnessLow
517	Spring.StiffnessVeryLow
518	```
519	
520	### Easing curves (still available for non-spring)
521	
522	```kotlin
523	MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier              // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
524	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier            // important transitions
525	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // incoming elements
526	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // outgoing
527	```
528	
529	### Duration tokens
530	
531	```
532	short1 = 50ms
533	short2 = 100ms
534	short3 = 150ms
535	short4 = 200ms
536	medium1 = 250ms
537	medium2 = 300ms
538	medium3 = 350ms
539	medium4 = 400ms
540	long1 = 450ms
541	long2 = 500ms
542	long3 = 550ms
543	long4 = 600ms
544	extraLong1 = 700ms
545	extraLong2 = 800ms
546	extraLong3 = 900ms
547	extraLong4 = 1000ms
548	```
549	
550	Default for UI feedback: `short3` (150ms) to `medium1` (250ms).
551	
552	### When to use spring vs easing
553	
554	- **Spring**: drag, gesture release, shape morphing, important state changes.
555	- **Easing**: enter/exit, predictable transitions, simple property changes.
556	
557	---
558	
559	## Shape System
560	
561	M3 has a shape system with five named tokens:
562	
563	```
564	extraSmall = 4dp
565	small = 8dp
566	medium = 12dp
567	large = 16dp
568	extraLarge = 28dp
569	full = 9999dp (pill)
570	```
571	
572	Applied per-component default:
573	- Buttons → full (pill)
574	- Cards → medium (12dp)
575	- Modals / sheets → extraLarge (28dp)
576	- Inputs → extraSmall (4dp)
577	- Snackbars → extraSmall
578	
579	In Compose:
580	```kotlin
581	Card(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium) { ... }
582	```
583	
584	---
585	
586	## Snackbars (the Toast equivalent)
587	
588	```kotlin
589	val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
590	val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()
591	
592	Scaffold(
593	  snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
594	) { padding ->
595	  Button(onClick = {
596	    scope.launch {
597	      snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
598	        message = "Project saved",
599	        actionLabel = "Undo",
600	        duration = SnackbarDuration.Short
601	      )
602	    }
603	  }) { Text("Save") }
604	}
605	```
606	
607	- Position: bottom of screen.
608	- Duration: Short (~4s) / Long (~7s) / Indefinite.
609	- One snackbar at a time.
610	- Includes action when reversible.
611	
612	---
613	
614	## Material You Dynamic Color
615	
616	Android 12+ supports user-wallpaper-derived themes. Opt in:
617	
618	```kotlin
619	val colorScheme = when {
620	  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
621	    val context = LocalContext.current
622	    if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
623	    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
624	  }
625	  darkTheme -> darkColorScheme()
626	  else -> lightColorScheme()
627	}
628	```
629	
630	For apps where brand identity is critical, **don't** use dynamic color — provide a
631	fixed `ColorScheme`. For consumer apps where personalization is welcome (Calendar,
632	Notes, Messages), opt in.
633	
634	---
635	
636	## The 15 Android Mobile Rules
637	
638	**1.** **48dp minimum tap targets.** Material guideline, hard floor.
639	
640	**2.** **Use Material Components**, don't reinvent buttons, sliders, switches.
641	
642	**3.** **Roboto Flex** as the default typeface; weight contrast > size contrast.
643	
644	**4.** **Pill-shaped buttons** as default (M3 Expressive).
645	
646	**5.** **Bottom navigation 64dp**, max 5 items, labels always visible.
647	
648	**6.** **Large flexible top app bars** for top-level destinations; small for drill-down.
649	
650	**7.** **Modal bottom sheets** for actions/filters, not centered dialogs.
651	
652	**8.** **Spring physics** for state-meaningful motion, not fixed easing.
653	
654	**9.** **Shape morphing on button press** (M3 Expressive default).
655	
656	**10.** **Dynamic color** for consumer apps; fixed scheme for brand-critical apps.
657	
658	**11.** **FAB Menu** for multi-action primary; FAB for single primary.
659	
660	**12.** **Floating Toolbars** for contextual action sets (deprecated Bottom App Bar).
661	
662	**13.** **Material 3 list item heights** strict: 48 / 56 / 64 / 72 / 88dp.
663	
664	**14.** **TalkBack labels** on every Icon-only button (`contentDescription`).
665	
666	**15.** **Test with TalkBack on**, large font size (200%), and dark theme.
667	
668	---
669	
670	## Flutter Material (cross-platform Android target)
671	
672	```dart
673	MaterialApp(
674	  theme: ThemeData(
675	    useMaterial3: true,
676	    colorSchemeSeed: Color(0xFF5E6AD2),
677	    typography: Typography.material2021(),
678	  ),
679	  home: Scaffold(
680	    appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Home')),
681	    body: ListView(
682	      children: [
683	        ListTile(
684	          title: Text('Item'),
685	          trailing: Icon(Icons.chevron_right),
686	        ),
687	      ],
688	    ),
689	    floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
690	      onPressed: () { },
691	      child: Icon(Icons.add),
692	    ),
693	    bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
694	      destinations: [
695	        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.home), label: 'Home'),
696	        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.search), label: 'Search'),
697	      ],
698	      selectedIndex: 0,
699	      onDestinationSelected: (i) { },
700	    ),
701	  ),
702	)
703	```
704	
705	Flutter's M3 support as of 2026 includes most M3 Expressive components, with FAB
706	Menu and Floating Toolbar landing in 2025–2026 updates.
707	
708	---
709	
710	## Apple vs Material — The Contradictions Table
711	
712	Cross-platform apps must respect platform conventions. Here's where the systems
713	diverge:
714	
715	| Concern | iOS | Material 3 |
716	|---|---|---|
717	| Primary action position | Trailing (right) in nav | Bottom right (FAB) or right in app bar |
718	| Modal style | Bottom sheet with detents | Modal bottom sheet OR dialog |
719	| Back navigation | Top-left chevron + label | Top-left arrow icon |
720	| Top nav title | Large title that collapses | Small or Large Flexible app bar |
721	| Tap target | 44pt | 48dp |
722	| Font | SF Pro variable | Roboto Flex variable |
723	| Hierarchy driver | Size + weight (Dynamic Type) | Weight > size (Bold over Big) |
724	| Button shape default | Capsule (`.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`) | Pill |
725	| Motion default | Smooth ease | Spring physics |
726	| Tab bar height | ~49pt (now glass, minimize on scroll) | 64dp (down from 80dp) |
727	| Empty space treatment | Generous | Slightly tighter |
728	| Color generation | Custom or system blue | Material You from wallpaper |
729	
730	For cross-platform: provide a platform-aware shim layer. Don't ship Material UI to
731	iOS or Cupertino UI to Android.
732	
733	---
734	
735	## Hard Bans for Android Pack
736	
737	- ❌ iOS-style centered dialogs on Android (use bottom sheets).
738	- ❌ Tap targets below 48dp.
739	- ❌ Hardcoded colors that ignore Material You / dynamic theming.
740	- ❌ Bottom app bars (deprecated in M3 Expressive; use Docked/Floating Toolbar).
741	- ❌ Old M3 navigation bar heights (80dp) — use 64dp.
742	- ❌ Bold selected labels in nav bar (M3 Expressive changed this default).
743	- ❌ Fixed-duration easing for state-meaningful transitions (use springs).
744	- ❌ Pre-Roboto-Flex fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans) when Roboto Flex is available.
745	- ❌ Ignoring Dynamic Type / font scale settings.
746	- ❌ Snackbars stacking (one at a time, latest wins).
747	- ❌ FABs that don't expand to FAB Menu when multiple actions exist.
748	- ❌ Custom toggles / sliders when Material variants suffice.
749

# Industry Pack — Mobile Android (Material 3 Expressive)

For Android apps built with Jetpack Compose or XML views, and Flutter apps using
Material widgets. Anchored to **Material 3 Expressive**, announced at the
**Android Show I/O Edition** on **May 13, 2025**, with general availability in
2025–2026 across Android 16, Wear OS 6, and Material Components.

Reference points: Google's flagship apps (Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps,
Messages, Drive, YouTube), **Material You** showcases, **Linear Android**,
**Notion Android**, **Spotify**, **Twitter/X**, **TickTick, Todoist**, **Pocket
Casts, Plex, Tasker, Microsoft Outlook for Android**.

---

## Pack Identity

Material 3 Expressive emphasizes:

- **Spring-based motion** as the default (replacing fixed easing curves)
- **Shape morphing** — components change shape on press (pill → rounded square)
- **Larger, bolder typography** with weight variation as the primary hierarchy
  driver (Bold over Big)
- **Color expressiveness** via dynamic Material You palette generation
- **Floating Toolbars / FAB Menus** replacing bottom app bars
- **Pill-shaped buttons** as the new default
- **5 button sizes** (XS / S / M / L / XL)
- **48dp minimum tap target** (always)
- **Navigation bar now 64dp** (down from 80dp in Material 3 stock)

---

## Token Overrides

```css
:root[data-pack="android"] {
  /* M3 dynamic color — use the user's wallpaper-based primary by default */
  --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.16 280);          /* default purple, will be overridden by Material You */
  --color-accent-fg: oklch(99% 0.01 280);
  --color-accent-soft: oklch(95% 0.04 280);
  --color-accent-strong: oklch(50% 0.18 280);

  /* M3 radii */
  --radius-button: 9999px;                      /* pill */
  --radius-input: 0.25rem;                      /* 4dp */
  --radius-card: 0.75rem;                       /* 12dp */
  --radius-modal: 1.75rem;                      /* 28dp - M3 modal corner */
  --radius-bottomsheet: 1.75rem;                /* 28dp top corner only */

  /* Roboto Flex variable */
  --font-sans: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-display: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;

  /* M3 leading */
  --leading-display: 1.12;
  --leading-headline: 1.25;
  --leading-title: 1.4;
  --leading-body: 1.45;
  --leading-label: 1.3;
}
```

For pure Material You (wallpaper-driven):
```css
:root[data-pack="android-you"] {
  --color-accent: oklch(var(--m3-primary));     /* sourced from system at runtime */
}
```

---

## The Material 3 Color System

M3 introduces **roles** instead of named colors. Each role has an `on*` companion
(for text/icon on that surface) and `*-container` variants (for backgrounds that
sit on top of the base).

### Primary palette

```
primary               — primary brand surface color (e.g., FAB background)
onPrimary             — text/icon on primary
primaryContainer      — softer container holding primary content
onPrimaryContainer    — text on primary container
```

Same pattern for `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `inverseSurface`.

### Full M3 Color Roles

```
primary, onPrimary, primaryContainer, onPrimaryContainer
secondary, onSecondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer
tertiary, onTertiary, tertiaryContainer, onTertiaryContainer
error, onError, errorContainer, onErrorContainer
background, onBackground
surface, onSurface
surfaceVariant, onSurfaceVariant
surfaceDim, surfaceBright
surfaceContainerLowest, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer,
  surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest
inverseSurface, inverseOnSurface, inversePrimary
outline, outlineVariant
scrim, shadow
```

13-tone palettes generate these from a single source color. With **Material You**,
that source color comes from the user's wallpaper at runtime.

### 3:1 contrast minimum for roles

All `on*` colors guarantee 3:1 contrast against their base. For body text use
`onSurface` on `surface` (always passes 4.5:1).

### In Compose

```kotlin
MaterialTheme(
  colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme(),
  typography = Typography(),
) {
  Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface) {
    Text("Hello", color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface)
  }
}
```

For dynamic Material You:
```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  isSystemInDarkTheme() -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

---

## Typography — The 15-Token Scale

M3 has 15 typography tokens (5 roles × 3 sizes). Apply via `MaterialTheme.typography`.

| Token | Size | Weight | Line height | Letter spacing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Display Large** | 57sp | Regular 400 | 64sp | -0.25 |
| **Display Medium** | 45sp | Regular 400 | 52sp | 0 |
| **Display Small** | 36sp | Regular 400 | 44sp | 0 |
| **Headline Large** | 32sp | Regular 400 | 40sp | 0 |
| **Headline Medium** | 28sp | Regular 400 | 36sp | 0 |
| **Headline Small** | 24sp | Regular 400 | 32sp | 0 |
| **Title Large** | 22sp | Regular 400 | 28sp | 0 |
| **Title Medium** | 16sp | Medium 500 | 24sp | 0.15 |
| **Title Small** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
| **Body Large** | 16sp | Regular 400 | 24sp | 0.5 |
| **Body Medium** | 14sp | Regular 400 | 20sp | 0.25 |
| **Body Small** | 12sp | Regular 400 | 16sp | 0.4 |
| **Label Large** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
| **Label Medium** | 12sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |
| **Label Small** | 11sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |

In Compose:
```kotlin
Text("Title", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
Text("Body copy", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
Text("Button", style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge)
```

### Roboto Flex variable

M3 Expressive (2025) ships **Roboto Flex** as the primary typeface — variable axes:
- Weight: 100–1000
- Width: 25–151%
- Optical size: 8–144
- Slant, grade, ascender height, descender depth, counter width, all variable

The "Bold over Big" principle: use weight (500 → 700) to convey hierarchy on the
same scale, instead of jumping size tokens.

### Display Flexible Variants (M3 Expressive only)

New in 2025: "Display Medium Flexible" and "Display Large Flexible" let apps use
larger, more expressive typography for product moments. Used in Google's flagship
apps for empty states, onboarding, hero moments.

---

## Buttons — 5 Sizes, 5 Styles

M3 Expressive ships **5 button sizes** and **5 button styles**.

### Sizes

| Size | Height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **XS** | 32dp | Inline, dense lists, chips-adjacent |
| **S** | 36dp | Secondary actions in tight spaces |
| **M** | 40dp | Default |
| **L** | 48dp | Primary actions, mobile CTAs |
| **XL** | 56dp | Hero CTAs, "Continue" in onboarding |

```kotlin
Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Default M") }
Button(onClick = { }, modifier = Modifier.height(48.dp)) { Text("L") }
Button(
  onClick = { },
  modifier = Modifier.height(56.dp),
  contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 24.dp),
) { Text("XL") }
```

### Styles

| Style | Background | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Filled** | `primary` | Primary action per screen |
| **Filled Tonal** | `secondaryContainer` | Co-equal action, softer than filled |
| **Elevated** | `surface` + shadow | Action that needs to lift off background |
| **Outlined** | transparent + outline | Secondary action |
| **Text** | transparent | Lowest-emphasis action, links |

```kotlin
Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Filled") }              // primary
FilledTonalButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Tonal") }    // secondary
ElevatedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Elevated") }
OutlinedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Outlined") }
TextButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Text") }
```

### Pill shape default, shape-morphs on press

M3 Expressive defaults all buttons to pill shape. On press, the shape morphs to
a slightly more rounded square via spring animation. The default is enabled when
using `ButtonDefaults.shape`.

```kotlin
Button(
  onClick = { },
  shape = ButtonDefaults.shape       // pill, morphs on press
) { Text("Action") }
```

### Icon buttons

```kotlin
IconButton(onClick = { }) {
  Icon(Icons.Default.Settings, contentDescription = "Settings")
}

// Toggleable
IconToggleButton(checked = isChecked, onCheckedChange = { isChecked = it }) {
  Icon(
    if (isChecked) Icons.Filled.Favorite else Icons.Outlined.FavoriteBorder,
    contentDescription = "Like"
  )
}
```

48dp tap target minimum. Always provide `contentDescription` for TalkBack.

---

## Navigation Bar (Bottom Nav)

Material 3 Expressive: **64dp height** (reduced from M3 standard 80dp). Active
indicator: 56dp pill behind the selected icon.

```kotlin
NavigationBar(modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp)) {
  navItems.forEach { item ->
    NavigationBarItem(
      icon = { Icon(item.icon, contentDescription = item.label) },
      label = { Text(item.label) },
      selected = currentRoute == item.route,
      onClick = { navigate(item.route) }
    )
  }
}
```

### Behaviors

- Active label not bold by default (M3 Expressive change — was bold in original M3).
- Labels always visible (selected and unselected).
- 3–5 items max. >5 items: use Navigation Drawer or Navigation Rail.

### Material You Color

Selected item indicator uses `secondaryContainer`. Icons use `onSurfaceVariant`
(unselected) → `onSecondaryContainer` (selected).

---

## Top App Bars

Four variants:

| Variant | Height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Small** | 64dp | Default for nested screens |
| **Center-aligned Small** | 64dp | Title centered (Material You style) |
| **Medium Flexible** | ~112dp | Important pages with extra space |
| **Large Flexible** | ~152dp | Hero pages, top-level destinations |

```kotlin
// Small top app bar
TopAppBar(
  title = { Text("Inbox") },
  navigationIcon = {
    IconButton(onClick = { /* back */ }) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowBack, contentDescription = "Back")
    }
  },
  actions = {
    IconButton(onClick = { /* search */ }) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.Search, contentDescription = "Search")
    }
  }
)

// Large top app bar that collapses on scroll
LargeTopAppBar(
  title = { Text("Inbox", style = MaterialTheme.typography.displaySmall) },
  scrollBehavior = scrollBehavior
)
```

### Scroll behaviors

- `pinnedScrollBehavior` — stays at top
- `enterAlwaysScrollBehavior` — collapses on scroll down, reappears on scroll up
- `exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior` — collapses to small variant, large only at top

Large Flexible is the equivalent of iOS's "large title" — big at top, collapses
to small on scroll.

---

## Bottom Sheets

Two variants:

### Standard Bottom Sheet

Inline with content (e.g., Google Maps location details). Always visible at
collapsed state, expands on drag.

```kotlin
BottomSheetScaffold(
  sheetContent = { LocationDetails() },
  sheetPeekHeight = 128.dp,
) { padding ->
  MapView(padding)
}
```

### Modal Bottom Sheet

Overlay with scrim. Used for actions, filters, share sheets.

```kotlin
val sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState()
val coroutineScope = rememberCoroutineScope()

ModalBottomSheet(
  onDismissRequest = { coroutineScope.launch { sheetState.hide() } },
  sheetState = sheetState,
  dragHandle = { BottomSheetDefaults.DragHandle() }
) {
  FilterContent()
}
```

Rounded top corners (28dp). Drag handle visible by default. Swipe-down dismisses.

---

## FAB and FAB Menu (NEW in M3 Expressive)

### Floating Action Button

```kotlin
FloatingActionButton(onClick = { compose() }) {
  Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, contentDescription = "Compose")
}

// Extended (with text)
ExtendedFloatingActionButton(
  onClick = { compose() },
  icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, null) },
  text = { Text("Compose") }
)

// Small / Large variants
SmallFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
LargeFloatingActionButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(...) }
```

### FAB Menu (NEW)

When a single action isn't enough, FAB expands into a menu of secondary actions.
M3 Expressive introduces this as a stock component.

```kotlin
FloatingActionButtonMenu(
  expanded = expanded,
  button = {
    ToggleFloatingActionButton(
      checked = expanded,
      onCheckedChange = { expanded = it }
    ) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.Add, null)
    }
  }
) {
  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Email, null) }, text = { Text("Email") })
  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Call, null) }, text = { Text("Call") })
  FloatingActionButtonMenuItem(onClick = { }, icon = { Icon(Icons.Default.Message, null) }, text = { Text("Message") })
}
```

Replaces the older "speed dial" pattern.

---

## Toolbars — Docked and Floating (NEW)

M3 Expressive deprecates the Bottom App Bar in favor of:

### Docked Toolbar

```kotlin
DockedToolbar(
  modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp),
  navigationIcon = { IconButton(...) { Icon(...) } },
  actions = {
    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, null) }
    IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.MoreVert, null) }
  }
)
```

### Floating Toolbar

Translucent material, floats above content like iOS Liquid Glass equivalent.

```kotlin
FloatingToolbar(
  modifier = Modifier
    .align(Alignment.BottomCenter)
    .padding(16.dp)
) {
  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatBold, null) }
  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatItalic, null) }
  IconButton(onClick = { }) { Icon(Icons.Default.FormatUnderlined, null) }
}
```

Use for: text editor formatting bars, contextual action sets, media player controls.

---

## Lists

### List Item Spec (M3)

| Lines | Height (no avatar) | Height (with avatar) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 line | 48dp | 56dp |
| 2 lines | 64dp | 72dp |
| 3 lines | 88dp | 88dp |

Always 16dp horizontal padding.

```kotlin
ListItem(
  headlineContent = { Text("Project Apollo") },
  supportingContent = { Text("Last updated 3 hours ago") },
  leadingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.Folder, null) },
  trailingContent = { Icon(Icons.Default.ChevronRight, null) },
  modifier = Modifier.clickable { open() }
)
```

### Dividers

Use `HorizontalDivider()` between sections, not between every item. Material 3
deprecated the always-divided list in favor of section-only dividers.

---

## Motion — Springs Replace Easing

M3 Expressive replaces fixed-duration easing with **spring physics tokens** as the
default for important transitions.

### Spring tokens

```kotlin
// In Compose, the default for state animations
spring<Float>(
  dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy,
  stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMedium
)

// Categories
Spring.DampingRatioHighBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy

Spring.StiffnessHigh
Spring.StiffnessMedium
Spring.StiffnessMediumLow
Spring.StiffnessLow
Spring.StiffnessVeryLow
```

### Easing curves (still available for non-spring)

```kotlin
MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier              // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier            // important transitions
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // incoming elements
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // outgoing
```

### Duration tokens

```
short1 = 50ms
short2 = 100ms
short3 = 150ms
short4 = 200ms
medium1 = 250ms
medium2 = 300ms
medium3 = 350ms
medium4 = 400ms
long1 = 450ms
long2 = 500ms
long3 = 550ms
long4 = 600ms
extraLong1 = 700ms
extraLong2 = 800ms
extraLong3 = 900ms
extraLong4 = 1000ms
```

Default for UI feedback: `short3` (150ms) to `medium1` (250ms).

### When to use spring vs easing

- **Spring**: drag, gesture release, shape morphing, important state changes.
- **Easing**: enter/exit, predictable transitions, simple property changes.

---

## Shape System

M3 has a shape system with five named tokens:

```
extraSmall = 4dp
small = 8dp
medium = 12dp
large = 16dp
extraLarge = 28dp
full = 9999dp (pill)
```

Applied per-component default:
- Buttons → full (pill)
- Cards → medium (12dp)
- Modals / sheets → extraLarge (28dp)
- Inputs → extraSmall (4dp)
- Snackbars → extraSmall

In Compose:
```kotlin
Card(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium) { ... }
```

---

## Snackbars (the Toast equivalent)

```kotlin
val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()

Scaffold(
  snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
) { padding ->
  Button(onClick = {
    scope.launch {
      snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
        message = "Project saved",
        actionLabel = "Undo",
        duration = SnackbarDuration.Short
      )
    }
  }) { Text("Save") }
}
```

- Position: bottom of screen.
- Duration: Short (~4s) / Long (~7s) / Indefinite.
- One snackbar at a time.
- Includes action when reversible.

---

## Material You Dynamic Color

Android 12+ supports user-wallpaper-derived themes. Opt in:

```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  darkTheme -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

For apps where brand identity is critical, **don't** use dynamic color — provide a
fixed `ColorScheme`. For consumer apps where personalization is welcome (Calendar,
Notes, Messages), opt in.

---

## The 15 Android Mobile Rules

**1.** **48dp minimum tap targets.** Material guideline, hard floor.

**2.** **Use Material Components**, don't reinvent buttons, sliders, switches.

**3.** **Roboto Flex** as the default typeface; weight contrast > size contrast.

**4.** **Pill-shaped buttons** as default (M3 Expressive).

**5.** **Bottom navigation 64dp**, max 5 items, labels always visible.

**6.** **Large flexible top app bars** for top-level destinations; small for drill-down.

**7.** **Modal bottom sheets** for actions/filters, not centered dialogs.

**8.** **Spring physics** for state-meaningful motion, not fixed easing.

**9.** **Shape morphing on button press** (M3 Expressive default).

**10.** **Dynamic color** for consumer apps; fixed scheme for brand-critical apps.

**11.** **FAB Menu** for multi-action primary; FAB for single primary.

**12.** **Floating Toolbars** for contextual action sets (deprecated Bottom App Bar).

**13.** **Material 3 list item heights** strict: 48 / 56 / 64 / 72 / 88dp.

**14.** **TalkBack labels** on every Icon-only button (`contentDescription`).

**15.** **Test with TalkBack on**, large font size (200%), and dark theme.

---

## Flutter Material (cross-platform Android target)

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorSchemeSeed: Color(0xFF5E6AD2),
    typography: Typography.material2021(),
  ),
  home: Scaffold(
    appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Home')),
    body: ListView(
      children: [
        ListTile(
          title: Text('Item'),
          trailing: Icon(Icons.chevron_right),
        ),
      ],
    ),
    floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
      onPressed: () { },
      child: Icon(Icons.add),
    ),
    bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
      destinations: [
        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.home), label: 'Home'),
        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.search), label: 'Search'),
      ],
      selectedIndex: 0,
      onDestinationSelected: (i) { },
    ),
  ),
)
```

Flutter's M3 support as of 2026 includes most M3 Expressive components, with FAB
Menu and Floating Toolbar landing in 2025–2026 updates.

---

## Apple vs Material — The Contradictions Table

Cross-platform apps must respect platform conventions. Here's where the systems
diverge:

| Concern | iOS | Material 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Primary action position | Trailing (right) in nav | Bottom right (FAB) or right in app bar |
| Modal style | Bottom sheet with detents | Modal bottom sheet OR dialog |
| Back navigation | Top-left chevron + label | Top-left arrow icon |
| Top nav title | Large title that collapses | Small or Large Flexible app bar |
| Tap target | 44pt | 48dp |
| Font | SF Pro variable | Roboto Flex variable |
| Hierarchy driver | Size + weight (Dynamic Type) | Weight > size (Bold over Big) |
| Button shape default | Capsule (`.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`) | Pill |
| Motion default | Smooth ease | Spring physics |
| Tab bar height | ~49pt (now glass, minimize on scroll) | 64dp (down from 80dp) |
| Empty space treatment | Generous | Slightly tighter |
| Color generation | Custom or system blue | Material You from wallpaper |

For cross-platform: provide a platform-aware shim layer. Don't ship Material UI to
iOS or Cupertino UI to Android.

---

## Hard Bans for Android Pack

- ❌ iOS-style centered dialogs on Android (use bottom sheets).
- ❌ Tap targets below 48dp.
- ❌ Hardcoded colors that ignore Material You / dynamic theming.
- ❌ Bottom app bars (deprecated in M3 Expressive; use Docked/Floating Toolbar).
- ❌ Old M3 navigation bar heights (80dp) — use 64dp.
- ❌ Bold selected labels in nav bar (M3 Expressive changed this default).
- ❌ Fixed-duration easing for state-meaningful transitions (use springs).
- ❌ Pre-Roboto-Flex fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans) when Roboto Flex is available.
- ❌ Ignoring Dynamic Type / font scale settings.
- ❌ Snackbars stacking (one at a time, latest wins).
- ❌ FABs that don't expand to FAB Menu when multiple actions exist.
- ❌ Custom toggles / sliders when Material variants suffice.

content.content:
1	# Motion
2	
3	Motion either elevates a UI or destroys it. The default position is **less, slower,
4	and only where meaning changes**. This file codifies Rauno Freiberg's interaction
5	principles and Emil Kowalski's animation rules into actionable defaults.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## The First Principle
10	
11	**Animation signals change.** If nothing has changed (state, location, focus, value),
12	nothing should animate. Decorative motion is noise.
13	
14	The corollary: **frequency kills delight.** Anything triggered hundreds of times a
15	day should be instant. Anything triggered once or twice a session can afford
16	personality.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## Emil Kowalski's Rules
21	
22	Emil Kowalski (currently Linear web team; previously Vercel; built Sonner and Vaul;
23	runs animations.dev) wrote the most-cited essay on UI animation: emilkowal.ski/ui/great-animations.
24	
25	### Rule 1 — Never animate keyboard-initiated actions
26	
27	Raycast has **no open animation**. Why? Users open it hundreds of times per day.
28	Any animation, no matter how snappy, becomes friction at that frequency.
29	
30	Apply this to:
31	- Command palette (Cmd+K)
32	- Esc to close anything
33	- Cmd+/ for shortcuts panel
34	- Cmd+Enter to submit
35	- Tab through fields
36	- Arrow key navigation
37	
38	These should appear/dismiss/transition **instantly** (`--duration-instant: 0ms`).
39	
40	### Rule 2 — Animate only `transform` and `opacity`
41	
42	These are GPU-accelerated. The browser composites them on a separate layer without
43	triggering layout or paint.
44	
45	Banned (cause layout/paint):
46	- `width`, `height`, `padding`, `margin`
47	- `top`, `left`, `right`, `bottom`
48	- `font-size`
49	- `border-width`
50	
51	If you need to animate size, use `transform: scale()` and reset on completion. If
52	you need to animate position, use `transform: translate()`.
53	
54	Exception: `background-color` is paint-only (no layout) and is fine to animate at
55	low frequency.
56	
57	### Rule 3 — CSS for predetermined animations, JS for interruptible ones
58	
59	```css
60	/* Predetermined: button hover. CSS. */
61	button {
62	  transition: background-color 100ms ease;
63	}
64	
65	/* Predetermined: modal enter. CSS. */
66	.modal[data-state="open"] {
67	  animation: scale-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
68	}
69	```
70	
71	```tsx
72	// Interruptible: drag-to-dismiss sheet. JS (Framer Motion / Motion One).
73	<motion.div
74	  drag="y"
75	  dragConstraints={{ top: 0 }}
76	  animate={{ y: isOpen ? 0 : "100%" }}
77	/>
78	```
79	
80	CSS animations run off the main thread → smoother under JS load. JS animations are
81	necessary only when the user can interrupt (gestures, scroll-driven, spring physics).
82	
83	### Rule 4 — Modal + overlay share duration and easing
84	
85	If the modal animates over 200ms with `ease-out`, the overlay (backdrop scrim) must
86	also animate 200ms with `ease-out`. Elements that move together must *feel* together.
87	
88	```css
89	[data-radix-dialog-overlay],
90	[data-radix-dialog-content] {
91	  animation-duration: 200ms;
92	  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
93	}
94	```
95	
96	### Rule 5 — Springs feel natural because they don't have fixed durations
97	
98	A spring animation's duration depends on its physics (mass, stiffness, damping). The
99	animation ends when the simulation settles, not when a clock hits zero.
100	
101	This makes spring motion feel "alive" in a way fixed-duration easing can't. Use
102	springs for:
103	- Drag interactions (release → settle back)
104	- Playful UI moments (sticker reactions, like buttons)
105	- Anywhere physics is the metaphor (a sheet falling away)
106	
107	Don't use springs for:
108	- Anything that needs to complete in a known time (forms, error messages)
109	- Anything that interrupts every animation in flight
110	- Critical-path actions where unpredictable timing breaks flow
111	
112	---
113	
114	## Rauno Freiberg's Principles
115	
116	Rauno Freiberg (Staff Design Engineer at Vercel; author of "Invisible Details of
117	Interaction Design"; built `cmdk`, the command palette library with 38M+ weekly
118	npm downloads).
119	
120	### Robustness beats novelty
121	
122	> "If your UI only works 80% of the time, the perception of quality breaks."
123	
124	Test under stress:
125	- Fast scroll
126	- Low battery / reduced animation
127	- Slow network (transitions during data load)
128	- Rapid clicks / double-tap
129	- Tab away and back during an animation
130	- Reduced motion preference
131	
132	If a transition glitches in any of these scenarios, it's worse than no transition.
133	
134	### Disney's "Follow-Through and Overlapping Action"
135	
136	Disney's classic principle of animation: secondary elements lag behind primary ones.
137	The hand lands; the arm continues for a moment.
138	
139	In UI:
140	- A modal opens; its contents fade in 100ms after the modal frame.
141	- A list expands; items appear staggered, not simultaneously.
142	- A header slides in; the underline animates after.
143	
144	```css
145	.modal-content { animation-delay: 100ms; }
146	.list-item { animation-delay: calc(var(--index) * 30ms); }
147	```
148	
149	Use sparingly. Stagger >5 items becomes annoying.
150	
151	### Build in code, not Figma
152	
153	The material reveals truth. A spring animation in Figma is a smooth easing line.
154	A spring animation in React with Framer Motion has real physics and reacts to user
155	input.
156	
157	Prototype in code from the start. The friction of switching modes (Figma → code)
158	is greater than the friction of working in code with a hot-reload dev server.
159	
160	### Validate by exaggeration
161	
162	Build the animation 10× too strong, then dial back. If the goal is a subtle 4px
163	translateY hover, first try translateY(-20px). Now you know what's too much.
164	The right amount is between the original guess and the exaggeration.
165	
166	---
167	
168	## Easing Curves — When to Use Each
169	
170	```css
171	--ease-linear: linear;
172	--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
173	--ease-in: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);
174	--ease-fluid: cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
175	--ease-snappy: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
176	--ease-emphasized: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
177	--ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
178	--ease-anticipate: cubic-bezier(0.36, 0, 0.66, -0.56);
179	```
180	
181	| Curve | Shape | Use |
182	|---|---|---|
183	| `linear` | constant | Loaders, progress bars, color shifts |
184	| `ease-out` | fast → slow | **Default for enter animations** (element arrives and settles) |
185	| `ease-in` | slow → fast | Exit animations (element accelerates away) |
186	| `ease-fluid` | symmetric | Bidirectional toggles (collapse/expand) |
187	| `ease-snappy` | fast deceleration | Quick UI feedback (button press release) |
188	| `ease-emphasized` | Material 3 default | Important state changes on Android |
189	| `ease-spring` | overshoots, settles | Playful interactions (like button, drag release) |
190	| `ease-anticipate` | pulls back, then forward | Rare; comedic timing |
191	
192	### iOS system curves (SwiftUI)
193	
194	```swift
195	.animation(.smooth, value: state)        // default smooth ease
196	.animation(.snappy, value: state)        // fast feedback
197	.animation(.bouncy, value: state)        // playful spring
198	.animation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.825), value: state)
199	```
200	
201	### Material 3 motion tokens
202	
203	```kotlin
204	MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier        // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
205	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier      // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
206	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // for incoming elements
207	MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // for outgoing
208	```
209	
210	M3 Expressive (2025) replaced fixed durations with **spring tokens** as the default
211	for important transitions. Stiffer springs for fast UI feedback, looser for celebratory
212	moments.
213	
214	---
215	
216	## Duration Bands
217	
218	```css
219	--duration-instant: 0ms;
220	--duration-fast: 100ms;
221	--duration-normal: 200ms;
222	--duration-slow: 300ms;
223	--duration-marketing: 400ms;
224	```
225	
226	### When to use each
227	
228	**0ms (instant)** — Anything triggered >50× per session.
229	- Cmd+K opens
230	- Esc closes
231	- Frequently-used menus
232	- Keyboard arrow navigation
233	
234	**100ms (fast)** — Hover and color changes.
235	- Button hover background
236	- Link underline
237	- Border color shift on focus
238	- Icon color change
239	
240	**200ms (normal)** — Enter/exit and transforms.
241	- Modal/dialog enter
242	- Sheet/drawer slide in
243	- Dropdown open
244	- Tooltip appear (after 300ms delay)
245	- Toast appear
246	
247	**300ms (slow)** — Marketing-adjacent and important state changes.
248	- Page transitions (when used)
249	- Hero element reveals on scroll
250	- Optimistic state confirmation
251	
252	**400ms (marketing)** — Hero reveals, parallax, scroll-driven type animation.
253	- Reserved for marketing site moments. Never in product UI.
254	
255	### What "feels right" is shorter than you think
256	
257	Default human perception of UI motion:
258	- <100ms feels instantaneous
259	- 100–300ms feels responsive
260	- 300–500ms feels deliberate
261	- >500ms feels slow / cinematic
262	
263	When in doubt, **shorten**.
264	
265	---
266	
267	## Specific Component Motion
268	
269	### Button hover
270	
271	```css
272	button {
273	  transition: background-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
274	}
275	button:active {
276	  transform: scale(0.98);
277	  transition: transform 80ms ease-out;
278	}
279	```
280	
281	### Modal / Dialog enter
282	
283	```css
284	@keyframes scale-in {
285	  from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.95); }
286	  to   { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
287	}
288	.modal {
289	  animation: scale-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
290	}
291	```
292	
293	### Bottom sheet slide
294	
295	```css
296	@keyframes slide-up {
297	  from { transform: translateY(100%); }
298	  to   { transform: translateY(0); }
299	}
300	.sheet {
301	  animation: slide-up 250ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
302	}
303	```
304	
305	For draggable sheets (Vaul), use spring physics in JS, not CSS easing.
306	
307	### Toast appear
308	
309	```css
310	@keyframes toast-in {
311	  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px) scale(0.95); }
312	  to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
313	}
314	.toast {
315	  animation: toast-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
316	}
317	```
318	
319	### Tooltip
320	
321	Delay open: 300ms. Delay close: 0ms (closes instantly to feel responsive).
322	
323	```tsx
324	<TooltipProvider delayDuration={300} skipDelayDuration={100}>
325	```
326	
327	### Dropdown / Popover
328	
329	200ms enter, `ease-out`. No exit animation if the user clicks outside (instant
330	dismiss). 100ms exit if Esc-triggered.
331	
332	### List reorder (FLIP)
333	
334	When a list reorders, animate items to their new positions using the FLIP technique:
335	**F**irst, **L**ast, **I**nvert, **P**lay.
336	
337	```tsx
338	import { motion } from "framer-motion";
339	
340	<motion.div layout transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}>
341	  {items.map(item => (
342	    <motion.div key={item.id} layout>{item.text}</motion.div>
343	  ))}
344	</motion.div>
345	```
346	
347	### State change (idle → loading → success)
348	
349	Smooth crossfade:
350	```css
351	.state-transition {
352	  transition: opacity 150ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
353	}
354	```
355	
356	When the spinner replaces the label in a button, the button width doesn't change
357	(fixed min-width). The label opacity fades to 0 as spinner opacity fades to 1.
358	
359	---
360	
361	## Page Transitions
362	
363	**App pages: instant.** Don't animate route changes in a product. Users want to be
364	*at* the new page, not watch it arrive. The exception is a defined wizard flow with
365	explicit "next step" semantics.
366	
367	**Marketing pages: optional, subtle.** Fade-in over 200–300ms is the maximum. Slide-

# Motion

Motion either elevates a UI or destroys it. The default position is **less, slower,
and only where meaning changes**. This file codifies Rauno Freiberg's interaction
principles and Emil Kowalski's animation rules into actionable defaults.

---

## The First Principle

**Animation signals change.** If nothing has changed (state, location, focus, value),
nothing should animate. Decorative motion is noise.

The corollary: **frequency kills delight.** Anything triggered hundreds of times a
day should be instant. Anything triggered once or twice a session can afford
personality.

---

## Emil Kowalski's Rules

Emil Kowalski (currently Linear web team; previously Vercel; built Sonner and Vaul;
runs animations.dev) wrote the most-cited essay on UI animation: emilkowal.ski/ui/great-animations.

### Rule 1 — Never animate keyboard-initiated actions

Raycast has **no open animation**. Why? Users open it hundreds of times per day.
Any animation, no matter how snappy, becomes friction at that frequency.

Apply this to:
- Command palette (Cmd+K)
- Esc to close anything
- Cmd+/ for shortcuts panel
- Cmd+Enter to submit
- Tab through fields
- Arrow key navigation

These should appear/dismiss/transition **instantly** (`--duration-instant: 0ms`).

### Rule 2 — Animate only `transform` and `opacity`

These are GPU-accelerated. The browser composites them on a separate layer without
triggering layout or paint.

Banned (cause layout/paint):
- `width`, `height`, `padding`, `margin`
- `top`, `left`, `right`, `bottom`
- `font-size`
- `border-width`

If you need to animate size, use `transform: scale()` and reset on completion. If
you need to animate position, use `transform: translate()`.

Exception: `background-color` is paint-only (no layout) and is fine to animate at
low frequency.

### Rule 3 — CSS for predetermined animations, JS for interruptible ones

```css
/* Predetermined: button hover. CSS. */
button {
  transition: background-color 100ms ease;
}

/* Predetermined: modal enter. CSS. */
.modal[data-state="open"] {
  animation: scale-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}
```

```tsx
// Interruptible: drag-to-dismiss sheet. JS (Framer Motion / Motion One).
<motion.div
  drag="y"
  dragConstraints={{ top: 0 }}
  animate={{ y: isOpen ? 0 : "100%" }}
/>
```

CSS animations run off the main thread → smoother under JS load. JS animations are
necessary only when the user can interrupt (gestures, scroll-driven, spring physics).

### Rule 4 — Modal + overlay share duration and easing

If the modal animates over 200ms with `ease-out`, the overlay (backdrop scrim) must
also animate 200ms with `ease-out`. Elements that move together must *feel* together.

```css
[data-radix-dialog-overlay],
[data-radix-dialog-content] {
  animation-duration: 200ms;
  animation-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}
```

### Rule 5 — Springs feel natural because they don't have fixed durations

A spring animation's duration depends on its physics (mass, stiffness, damping). The
animation ends when the simulation settles, not when a clock hits zero.

This makes spring motion feel "alive" in a way fixed-duration easing can't. Use
springs for:
- Drag interactions (release → settle back)
- Playful UI moments (sticker reactions, like buttons)
- Anywhere physics is the metaphor (a sheet falling away)

Don't use springs for:
- Anything that needs to complete in a known time (forms, error messages)
- Anything that interrupts every animation in flight
- Critical-path actions where unpredictable timing breaks flow

---

## Rauno Freiberg's Principles

Rauno Freiberg (Staff Design Engineer at Vercel; author of "Invisible Details of
Interaction Design"; built `cmdk`, the command palette library with 38M+ weekly
npm downloads).

### Robustness beats novelty

> "If your UI only works 80% of the time, the perception of quality breaks."

Test under stress:
- Fast scroll
- Low battery / reduced animation
- Slow network (transitions during data load)
- Rapid clicks / double-tap
- Tab away and back during an animation
- Reduced motion preference

If a transition glitches in any of these scenarios, it's worse than no transition.

### Disney's "Follow-Through and Overlapping Action"

Disney's classic principle of animation: secondary elements lag behind primary ones.
The hand lands; the arm continues for a moment.

In UI:
- A modal opens; its contents fade in 100ms after the modal frame.
- A list expands; items appear staggered, not simultaneously.
- A header slides in; the underline animates after.

```css
.modal-content { animation-delay: 100ms; }
.list-item { animation-delay: calc(var(--index) * 30ms); }
```

Use sparingly. Stagger >5 items becomes annoying.

### Build in code, not Figma

The material reveals truth. A spring animation in Figma is a smooth easing line.
A spring animation in React with Framer Motion has real physics and reacts to user
input.

Prototype in code from the start. The friction of switching modes (Figma → code)
is greater than the friction of working in code with a hot-reload dev server.

### Validate by exaggeration

Build the animation 10× too strong, then dial back. If the goal is a subtle 4px
translateY hover, first try translateY(-20px). Now you know what's too much.
The right amount is between the original guess and the exaggeration.

---

## Easing Curves — When to Use Each

```css
--ease-linear: linear;
--ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
--ease-in: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1);
--ease-fluid: cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
--ease-snappy: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
--ease-emphasized: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
--ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);
--ease-anticipate: cubic-bezier(0.36, 0, 0.66, -0.56);
```

| Curve | Shape | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `linear` | constant | Loaders, progress bars, color shifts |
| `ease-out` | fast → slow | **Default for enter animations** (element arrives and settles) |
| `ease-in` | slow → fast | Exit animations (element accelerates away) |
| `ease-fluid` | symmetric | Bidirectional toggles (collapse/expand) |
| `ease-snappy` | fast deceleration | Quick UI feedback (button press release) |
| `ease-emphasized` | Material 3 default | Important state changes on Android |
| `ease-spring` | overshoots, settles | Playful interactions (like button, drag release) |
| `ease-anticipate` | pulls back, then forward | Rare; comedic timing |

### iOS system curves (SwiftUI)

```swift
.animation(.smooth, value: state)        // default smooth ease
.animation(.snappy, value: state)        // fast feedback
.animation(.bouncy, value: state)        // playful spring
.animation(.spring(response: 0.5, dampingFraction: 0.825), value: state)
```

### Material 3 motion tokens

```kotlin
MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier        // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier      // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // for incoming elements
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // for outgoing
```

M3 Expressive (2025) replaced fixed durations with **spring tokens** as the default
for important transitions. Stiffer springs for fast UI feedback, looser for celebratory
moments.

---

## Duration Bands

```css
--duration-instant: 0ms;
--duration-fast: 100ms;
--duration-normal: 200ms;
--duration-slow: 300ms;
--duration-marketing: 400ms;
```

### When to use each

**0ms (instant)** — Anything triggered >50× per session.
- Cmd+K opens
- Esc closes
- Frequently-used menus
- Keyboard arrow navigation

**100ms (fast)** — Hover and color changes.
- Button hover background
- Link underline
- Border color shift on focus
- Icon color change

**200ms (normal)** — Enter/exit and transforms.
- Modal/dialog enter
- Sheet/drawer slide in
- Dropdown open
- Tooltip appear (after 300ms delay)
- Toast appear

**300ms (slow)** — Marketing-adjacent and important state changes.
- Page transitions (when used)
- Hero element reveals on scroll
- Optimistic state confirmation

**400ms (marketing)** — Hero reveals, parallax, scroll-driven type animation.
- Reserved for marketing site moments. Never in product UI.

### What "feels right" is shorter than you think

Default human perception of UI motion:
- <100ms feels instantaneous
- 100–300ms feels responsive
- 300–500ms feels deliberate
- >500ms feels slow / cinematic

When in doubt, **shorten**.

---

## Specific Component Motion

### Button hover

```css
button {
  transition: background-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
}
button:active {
  transform: scale(0.98);
  transition: transform 80ms ease-out;
}
```

### Modal / Dialog enter

```css
@keyframes scale-in {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.95); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
}
.modal {
  animation: scale-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}
```

### Bottom sheet slide

```css
@keyframes slide-up {
  from { transform: translateY(100%); }
  to   { transform: translateY(0); }
}
.sheet {
  animation: slide-up 250ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}
```

For draggable sheets (Vaul), use spring physics in JS, not CSS easing.

### Toast appear

```css
@keyframes toast-in {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(20px) scale(0.95); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0) scale(1); }
}
.toast {
  animation: toast-in 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
}
```

### Tooltip

Delay open: 300ms. Delay close: 0ms (closes instantly to feel responsive).

```tsx
<TooltipProvider delayDuration={300} skipDelayDuration={100}>
```

### Dropdown / Popover

200ms enter, `ease-out`. No exit animation if the user clicks outside (instant
dismiss). 100ms exit if Esc-triggered.

### List reorder (FLIP)

When a list reorders, animate items to their new positions using the FLIP technique:
**F**irst, **L**ast, **I**nvert, **P**lay.

```tsx
import { motion } from "framer-motion";

<motion.div layout transition={{ duration: 0.2 }}>
  {items.map(item => (
    <motion.div key={item.id} layout>{item.text}</motion.div>
  ))}
</motion.div>
```

### State change (idle → loading → success)

Smooth crossfade:
```css
.state-transition {
  transition: opacity 150ms cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
}
```

When the spinner replaces the label in a button, the button width doesn't change
(fixed min-width). The label opacity fades to 0 as spinner opacity fades to 1.

---

## Page Transitions

**App pages: instant.** Don't animate route changes in a product. Users want to be
*at* the new page, not watch it arrive. The exception is a defined wizard flow with
explicit "next step" semantics.

**Marketing pages: optional, subtle.** Fade-in over 200–300ms is the maximum. Slide-
in transitions are heavy and dated.

### Next.js App Router with View Transitions API

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
<html style={{ viewTransitionName: "root" }}>
```

```css
::view-transition-old(root),
::view-transition-new(root) {
  animation-duration: 250ms;
}
```

Use sparingly. The default no-animation is correct for 90% of routes.

---

## Scroll-Driven Animation

Modern browsers support `animation-timeline: scroll()` and `animation-timeline: view()`.
Use these for marketing reveals.

```css
@keyframes fade-up {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(40px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
}

.scroll-reveal {
  animation: fade-up linear;
  animation-timeline: view();
  animation-range: entry 10% cover 30%;
}
```

Rules:
- Trigger only once per scroll into view (don't replay on scroll up).
- Reveals only on marketing pages, never in product UI.
- Provide reduced-motion fallback (just appear, no animation).
- Don't reveal the entire page chunk-by-chunk — pick 2–3 hero moments.

---

## Reduced Motion

```css
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  *, *::before, *::after {
    animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
    transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
    scroll-behavior: auto !important;
  }
}
```

Don't disable everything. Keep:
- Opacity transitions (≤100ms) — needed for state change clarity.
- Background color transitions — needed for hover feedback.

Disable:
- All `transform` animations.
- Scroll-driven reveals.
- Parallax.
- Auto-playing video / GIF backgrounds.
- Spring physics.

### Test it

Toggle macOS System Settings → Accessibility → Display → Reduce Motion. The UI
should still be perfectly usable, just stiller. If it feels broken without motion,
the motion was hiding bad design.

---

## Anti-Patterns

### Don't animate frequently-triggered actions
- Dropdown menu open on a primary nav button (clicked 30× a session) → instant.
- Filter pill toggle (clicked 50× a session) → instant.
- "Mark as read" toast (appears 100× a session) → instant or very short (≤100ms).

### Don't stagger >5 items
Stagger is delightful at 2–4 items. At 6+, it feels like waiting. List items should
animate together (or use FLIP for individual position changes).

### Don't use spring physics for forms
Form submission feedback should complete in known time. A bouncy success message
that overshoots makes users second-guess whether the action worked. Use ease-out.

### Don't auto-animate on enter
The single most-overused effect in 2020s web design: every section fades + slides in
as the user scrolls past. By 2025, this signals "template" or "AI-generated."

Pick **one** hero moment per marketing page that earns a reveal. Everything else is static.

### Don't animate scroll-jacking
Forced scroll snapping, scroll-hijacked horizontal sections, "story mode" navigation
that traps the user — all hostile. Let scroll be scroll.

### Don't combine multiple motion types

```css
/* Wrong: opacity + scale + translate + rotate */
.bad {
  animation: opacity-in 200ms, scale-in 200ms, slide-up 200ms, rotate-in 200ms;
}
```

Two properties max in any single animation. Three when one is opacity for
crossfading.

---

## Library Recommendations

| Library | When to use |
|---|---|
| **CSS** (built-in) | 80% of animations. Default. |
| **Framer Motion** (now "Motion") | Drag, gesture, layout animations, complex orchestration |
| **Motion One** | Lightweight web alternative to Framer Motion |
| **Vaul** (Emil Kowalski) | Mobile bottom sheets with drag-to-dismiss |
| **Sonner** (Emil Kowalski) | Toasts |
| **cmdk** (Paco Coursey / Rauno Freiberg) | Command palette |
| **AutoAnimate** (FormKit) | Drop-in list animations (FLIP) without setup |
| **GSAP** | Complex marketing storytelling, scroll-driven cinema |
| **View Transitions API** | Native page transitions, modern browsers |

For Grain's default stack: CSS + Framer Motion + Vaul + Sonner + cmdk.

---

## The Self-Check Before Adding Any Animation

Ask:
1. **Does something change?** If no, no animation.
2. **How often is this triggered?** >50/session = instant.
3. **Is the user waiting for an outcome?** Then shorten or remove.
4. **Does it work under reduced-motion?** Test it.
5. **Does it work at 60fps on a 4-year-old phone?** If you can't verify, simplify.
6. **Is it `transform` and/or `opacity` only?** If not, refactor.
7. **Would Rauno or Emil ship this?** If you can't argue yes with a straight face,
   simplify.

If three or more of these fail, remove the animation entirely. No motion beats bad motion.
